experiments.title: Geometry probe for affordance segmentation
experiments.question: Do geometry-aware VFM representations make affordance segmentation linearly separable?
experiments.hypothesis: If affordance reasoning needs geometric primitives, VFMs with stronger part-level geometry should score higher on UMD mIoU, and explicit depth or surface-normal cues should help models with weaker geometric priors.
experiments.benchmark: UMD affordance segmentation; AGD20K remains target for local follow-up
experiments.dataset: UMD, seven affordance categories, 11,800 training images, 14,020 testing images
baselines: frozen VFM features plus surface normals
protocol: Extract and fuse four equally spaced ViT layers where applicable.
Train a BatchNorm plus 1x1 Conv linear head with cross-entropy loss.
Evaluate UMD affordance mask prediction with mIoU.
Concatenate Metric3Dv2 depth and surface-normal cues to test whether explicit 3D signals improve each backbone.
experiments.expected_evidence: Geometry-aware models should produce stronger mIoU and more coherent part-level PCA structure; depth and normals should improve semantic models more than DINO-family models.
risks: Linear probing measures separability, not causal affordance understanding.
UMD masks are categorical affordance labels, not verb-conditioned interaction heatmaps.
This is imported paper evidence and is not reproduced in the local workspace.
experiments.next_action: Reproduce the UMD probe locally or use it as the geometry-only control for the AGD20K fusion reproduction.

experiments.title: Verb-conditioned interaction prior from Flux Kontext
experiments.question: Can verb-conditioned generative attention localize plausible contact regions without affordance-specific training?
experiments.hypothesis: If generative models encode interaction priors, Flux Kontext verb-token attention should align with action-bearing regions and produce useful zero-shot AGD20K affordance heatmaps.
experiments.dataset: AGD20K egocentric object images paired with exocentric interaction exemplars
protocol: Prompt the generative model with object and verb conditions.
Treat verb attention as a zero-shot affordance heatmap.
Compare against AGD20K ground-truth heatmaps and qualitative attention baselines.
experiments.expected_evidence: Flux Kontext verb attention should highlight physically plausible contact regions and approach weakly supervised affordance performance without task-specific training.
risks: Attention maps are proxy evidence, not direct action execution.
Generative output can fail even when attention stays spatially plausible.
Noun attention noise can pollute the object region used by the fusion pipeline.
experiments.next_action: Re-run verb-attention extraction on the demo AGD20K examples and save heatmap artifacts.

experiments.title: Training-free geometry-interaction fusion
experiments.question: Does composing DINOv3 geometry with Flux Kontext interaction attention improve zero-shot affordance localization?
experiments.hypothesis: If geometric and interaction primitives are complementary, selecting DINOv3 PCA geometry components aligned to Flux verb attention should outperform interaction-only heatmaps.
experiments.benchmark: AGD20K quantitative evaluation; UMD qualitative validation
experiments.dataset: AGD20K unseen egocentric objects for KLD/SIM/NSS; UMD categorical masks for qualitative part alignment
protocol: Use object attention to crop a DINOv3 region of interest.
Run PCA on ROI features to obtain part-level geometric bases.
Use Flux Kontext verb attention as the probable action region.
Compute NSS between each geometric basis and verb attention.
Select the best-aligned geometry component and fuse it with verb attention.
Evaluate on AGD20K and inspect UMD hold, cut, and drink examples.
experiments.expected_evidence: Interaction x Geometry should reduce KLD and improve SIM/NSS relative to Only Interaction, while UMD examples should align hold with handles, cut with blades, and drink with rims or openings.
risks: The result does not prove embodied causal understanding.
AGD20K and UMD only approximate richer action-object relations.
experiments.next_action: Make EXP3 the first local reproduction target and attach generated masks to each run.

experiments.title: Semantic assimilation control for geometry
experiments.question: Are DINO geometry correspondences pure shape evidence, or can object semantics suppress geometric matches?
experiments.hypothesis: If DINO geometry is entangled with global semantics, local shape correspondence should work in simplified scenes but weaken when the full object context is visible.
experiments.dataset: Paper qualitative control scenes containing ring-like shapes and full mug context
protocol: Select a mug-handle patch as the reference feature.
Compare activation over simplified ring-like shapes.
Compare activation over full-scene object context.
Use the failure mode to bound claims about pure geometric representation.
experiments.expected_evidence: Ring-like simplified shapes should activate from local geometry, while full scene context can suppress those responses through object semantics.
risks: Does not quantify how much semantic assimilation affects downstream affordance masks.
experiments.next_action: Add a local category-scrambling control to separate geometry, object semantics, and action contact evidence.
